steps.note: the API built this case's state
Use an RFQ pricing stage.
Configure the RFQ stage before selecting its template.
Apply the RFQ pricing template.
Create the single 10-unit line required for the 4/3/3 split.
Populate the RFQ pricing sheet.
Commit a bidding window before publishing.
Invite three distinct vendors for the three bids.
Submit the 100 bid for the first vendor.
Confirm the first vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit the 90 bid for the second vendor.
Confirm the second vendor's bid was accepted.
Submit the 95 bid for the third vendor.
Confirm the third vendor's bid was accepted.
Close the bidding round so awarding is available.
Open the comparison grid containing the three bids.
Enter the awarding screen where quantities can be allocated.

args.goal: On the awarding screen, allocate 4 units to the vendor bidding 90, 3 units to the vendor bidding 95, and 3 units to the vendor bidding 100; verify Awarded Vendors reads 3/3, create the proposal, fill its required fields, submit it, and stop on the submitted proposal showing amounts 360, 285, 300 and total 945.

steps.note: The catalog has no structured step for entering split quantities or completing the proposal fields, so perform and verify those buyer-side actions directly on screen.
Confirm the submitted award proposal page is open.
